pages.text: Rain had fallen for days. With the river high, laundry hung inside, stretching across the room.
The three children sat close in the narrow space. Mina poured blue beads into a bowl. "I'll finish this necklace today."
Sonu's hand kept reaching into Mina's bead bowl.
"You have some in yours!" Mina snatched Sonu's bowl and hid it behind their back. "Touch mine, and I won't give yours back!"
Sonu pushed Mina's back. Mina blocked with one hand and threaded beads with the other.
The thread slipped out. Beads rolled away.
They all went beneath the laundry and threshold. The necklace was short.
Taking in the laundry, Mom asked, "Both your hands were busy. What were you doing?"
Mina returned Sonu's bowl. Sonu lay flat to look beneath the threshold.
Sonu brought back a handful of beads. The necklace fitted Mina's neck just right.
